text_blocks.snippet: High cholesterol often does not present with noticeable symptoms. However, some subtle signs may indicate elevated cholesterol levels:

list.snippet: Corneal arcus: A grayish-white ring around the cornea of the eye.
Xanthelasma: Yellowish deposits on the eyelids or other areas of the skin.
Peripheral artery disease (PAD): Pain or cramping in the legs when walking or exercising.
Fatigue: High cholesterol can interfere with oxygen delivery to the body.
Chest pain: In severe cases, high cholesterol can cause blockages in the arteries supplying the heart.
